E25 Wire and onboard the sense board on screen

Goal. Draw a SENSE board's wiring on the onboarding wizard's screen, save it as a board template, onboard the board with it, and see its readings, its health message and its start-up test message arrive. Then unplug one sensor and see the board report it and carry on. The exercise proves the wiring screen (see Wiring a SENSE board on screen) and the decisions of 6 November 2026 "Health and test messages are stored" and "Hubs on one bus: the board closes the other hub's channel" (see the decision record). It also finishes step 6 of E22, with the board rewired as below.

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer) in the onboarding wizard and the MQTT Explorer; the host operator for the deploys and the checks on the server.

Before you start. The host operator has run, in this order, ./apps/database/deploy.sh (migration 009), ./apps/node-red/deploy.sh and ./apps/edge-wizard/deploy.sh (refused while a flash runs), and ./health-check.sh shows Node-RED's flows OK. The board is the ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 of E22, wired as the bench test of 6 November 2026 passed: one I2C bus on GPIO 8 (SDA) and GPIO 9 (SCL), a TCA9548A at 0x70 (the SparkFun Qwiic Mux; nothing else on the root bus), the SHT45 on hub channel 7 and the SCD30 on channel 6, every part on 3V3 and GND. The SEN0562 is optional: fit it on channel 2 (its colours as in DFRobot's wiki) if you have it, and add it in step 3. The slot is E22's (UNIT02 / ZONE01), so the run onboards the board again in place. Optional, and quickest when something does not answer: run the bench test on the board first, as in Check the wiring before onboarding, and start only when it prints ALL PASS (the onboarding erase replaces it on the board anyway).

Steps.

  1. eng: open https://onboard-device.<domain>, choose ESP32 / ESP32-S3, the role SENSE and the slot UNIT02 / ZONE01.
  2. At How is this board wired? choose Wire the sensors on screen. In Start from choose Sense board as bench-tested 6 Nov 2026: the board, the hub and the two sensors appear wired, with no findings.
  3. Check the wiring against the bench: click the board (SDA 8, SCL 9, the hardware driver, external pull-ups), the hub (0x70), and each sensor's channel (SHT45 7, SCD30 6). If the SEN0562 is fitted, click + DFRobot SEN0562 (IP68 ambient light) and wire it to channel 2.
  4. Click the SCD30: under Published as, only co2 is ticked. Try the refusals below, then undo each.
  5. Tick Save as a board template: name bench-sense-e25, title "E25 bench board". Click Continue, and let the run finish (interval, erase, WiFi).
  6. eng: open the MQTT Explorer and watch medcea/UNIT02/ZONE01/sense.
  7. Unplug the SHT45's cable at the hub, wait for a cycle, then plug it back.
  8. Host operator: python3 edge/src/host/device_template.py board-templates SENSE.

What you should see.

  • Steps 3 to 5: the findings list is empty once everything is wired (no hub warning once a sensor is on it); Continue is taken only then. The run's log names the board template saved.
  • Step 6, within a minute of the end of the run: _test ("source":"board-boot", the board's ip, mac and firmware), _health with every wired sensor "ok":true, then air_temperature, air_humidity and co2 (and light_intensity with the SEN0562) every interval. No co2 for the SCD30's first seconds is normal: it is warming up.
  • Step 7: a _health with sht45_1 (or the id the screen gave it) "ok":false and a reason in err; the other tags keep arriving and the board does not restart. Plugging it back, the next reading normally brings a _health with it "ok":true again (a sensor that was already missing at boot is tried again within 10 minutes).
  • Step 8: the two shipped templates and bench-sense-e25 with source saved and valid 1.

In the Devices tab: the device record of unit02-s-zone01 updated in place, with one component record per sensor (driver, address, bus pins, hub and channel, tags). In medcea.measurement: the readings (AP), the health messages (HB) and the start-up test (TS), readable as in E26. On the host: edge/provisioned/unit02-s-zone01.json with "wiring", and edge/board-templates/bench-sense-e25.json with "saved_by": "eng". Write the date, the board, the templates listed in step 8 and what steps 6 and 7 showed under Last done.

Refusals worth trying (step 4; each shows in the findings list and Continue does nothing):

  • A second SHT45 on channel 7 at its default address: "… answers 0x44, like … on the same segment." On another channel it is accepted, with its tags renamed.
  • The SCD30's temperature ticked as air_temperature: "air_temperature is already published by …: two sensors on one tag would interleave one series."
  • A tag renamed _health: ""_health" is not a tag name: a lower-case letter, then up to 47 letters, digits or _."
  • A sensor (for example a new SEN0562) left without a wire: "… is not wired: drag a wire from the board or hub to it."
  • GPIO 8 on an original ESP32 (the screen offers only the ESP32-S3, so on the host): python3 edge/src/host/device_template.py board-template sense-hub-bench-sht45-scd30 | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d["board"]={"variant":"esp32"}; print(json.dumps(d))' | python3 edge/src/host/device_template.py validate-wiring SENSE esp32; echo "exit $?": "GPIO8 is wired to the module's SPI flash. Driving it crashes the board." (and the same for GPIO 9), exit 1. A run with such a board stops after probing, before the erase.

Afterwards. Keep the board. Commit edge/board-templates/bench-sense-e25.json if the template is worth keeping, or delete the file.

Last done. 7 November 2026, partly, by the tester with eng; read back from the platform by the host operator. The ESP32-S3 a4:cb:8f:de:73:9c was onboarded at 07:39 UTC into UNIT01 / ZONE01 rather than E22's UNIT02 / ZONE01: the wizard moved device 1 there (device_slot_history event 9, moved from unit02-s-zone01 to unit01-s-zone01, by eng, source token). Its wiring as recorded (edge/provisioned/unit01-s-zone01.json, registered_by eng) is the bench template's: hardware I2C on GPIO 8 / 9 at 100 kHz, the hub at 0x70, the SHT45 (0x44) on channel 7 and the SCD30 (0x61) on channel 6; device 1 has two active component records, sht45_1 (channel 7, address 68) and scd30_1 (channel 6, address 97), and its six older components are inactive. Step 6: in medcea.measurement the start-up TS ("source":"board-boot", ip 192.168.1.159, mac a4:cb:8f:de:73:9c) and one HB with both sensors "ok":true at 07:41:53, then air_temperature, air_humidity and co2 every 6 seconds (159 readings by 07:47; means 22.7 °C, 50.2 %RH, 1062 ppm). Not done or left no trace: no board template was saved (step 5's Save as: edge/board-templates/ holds only its README); no _health with "ok":false (step 7, the unplugged SHT45, not seen); step 4's screen refusals not reported. Step 8, by the host operator at 07:51: the two shipped templates, both shipped and valid 1, and no saved one. The refusals checked on the host with validate-wiring on the bench template (the screen applies the same rules; parity-tested): a second SHT45 on channel 7 at 0x44 → E_ADDR_CLASH "sht45_2 answers 0x44, like sht45_1 on the same segment."; the SCD30's temperature as air_temperature → E_TAG_DUP "air_temperature is already published by sht45_1: …"; a tag _health → E_TAG; an unwired SEN0562 → E_UNWIRED "lux_1 is not wired: drag a wire from the board or hub to it."; GPIO 8 on esp32 → "GPIO8 is wired to the module's SPI flash. Driving it crashes the board." (and GPIO 9), exit 1. E26 Send a test message and find it

Goal. Send a test message as a board, from the wizard and from the host, and find it in the MQTT Explorer and in the database, together with the one the board sent at start-up. The exercise proves the decision of 6 November 2026 "Health and test messages are stored" (see the decision record) and the Send test message button (see Sending a test message).

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer) in the onboarding wizard, the MQTT Explorer and Grafana; a second account that onboarding admits (another engineer or maintenance), in its own browser session; the host operator at the server's terminal, in the repository folder.

Before you start. E25 done, with its wizard page still open on the finished run (or any run that registered a board since the deploys E25 names).

Steps.

  1. eng: in the MQTT Explorer, open medcea/UNIT02/ZONE01/sense/_test and read the start-up message.
  2. eng: on the wizard page of the finished run, click Send test message; click it again as soon as it can be clicked.
  3. The second account: open the wizard page.
  4. Host operator: ./edge/flash-device.sh --send-test unit02-s-zone01; echo "exit $?".
  5. Host operator: ./medcea.sh → Edge devices → Send a test message as a board, choose unit02-s-zone01, and confirm.
  6. eng: in Grafana, Explore, run SELECT measure_timestamp, device_dns, msg->>'source' AS source, msg->>'sent_from' AS sent_from FROM medcea.measurement WHERE msg_type = 'TS' ORDER BY measure_timestamp DESC LIMIT 20.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: "msg_type":"TS", "tag":"_test", "source":"board-boot", the board's ip, mac, firmware, device_id and device_dns.
  • Step 2: "Sent at <time> on medcea/UNIT02/ZONE01/sense/_test; look for tag _test in the MQTT Explorer.", and a new _test in the Explorer with "source":"wizard" and "sent_from":"host". The second click within 5 seconds: "One test message every 5 seconds — try again in a moment."
  • Step 3: no Send test message button: only the person who started the run gets it.
  • Step 4: "Sending a test message as unit02-s-zone01 to <address>:31884 (TLS, mqtt.<domain>)", then one line {"ok":true,"topic":"medcea/UNIT02/ZONE01/sense/_test",…} and exit 0; a _test with "source":"cli" in the Explorer.
  • Step 5: medcea.sh lists the registered boards with a record, shows the command, and after the confirmation the same result as step 4.
  • Step 6: one TS row per message of steps 1, 2, 4 and 5, with sources board-boot, wizard and cli; sent_from is empty for the board's own and host for the others.

Each test message is a TS row in medcea.measurement, which nobody edits or deletes. The wizard's log (journalctl --user -u cea-edge-wizard on the host) has "wizard: test message as unit02-s-zone01 by eng: <topic>", and never a password. Write the date and what steps 2, 4 and 6 showed under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • ./edge/flash-device.sh --send-test UNIT02: "--send-test: not a board name: 'UNIT02' (e.g. unit01-s-zone01)", exit 2.
  • ./edge/flash-device.sh --send-test unit09-s-zone09 (no such record): "--send-test: no readable record <repository>/edge/provisioned/unit09-s-zone09.json (onboard the board first)", exit 2.
  • ./edge/flash-device.sh --send-test unit02-s-zone01 --role SENSE: "--send-test flashes nothing: not with --role (only --mqtt-host, --mqtt-port, --mqtt-tls-name)", exit 2.
  • A test message whose payload claims "msg_type":"AP" is still stored as TS, because the type is taken from the topic. No person may publish on a board's topic yet (that waits for the MQTT Explorer path), so this is checked offline: python3 -m unittest tests.test_msg_types runs Node-RED's own function on it.

Afterwards. Nothing to undo: the test rows stay, as every measurement does.

Step 2: one Send test message from the finished run of E25: the wizard's log has wizard: test message as unit01-s-zone01 by eng: medcea/UNIT01/ZONE01/sense/_test at 07:39:17, the broker's log a TLS connection as unit01-s-zone01-test-a741 (user unit01-s-zone01) that disconnected at once, and the database a TS row with "source":"wizard" and "sent_from":"host"; the second click within 5 seconds was not reported. Step 5 at 07:50:17 through the guide, the same result ("Finished: exit code 0."). Refusals tried: --send-test UNIT01 → "not a board name", exit 2; a name without a record → "no readable record … (onboard the board first)", exit 2. Found while doing it: the guide also lists unit02-s-zone01, the record the board left behind when E25 moved it; sending as it is refused by the broker ("the broker refused the board's credential: not authorised", exit 1), correctly, since that credential was retired at the move, but the guide should not offer it. E27 Superset stage C: approve, apply and sign in

Goal. Take Superset's access policy through the only path it has, then install Superset and see that it admits exactly the roles the policy gives it. A skeleton version, proposed from a commit, adds Superset's host, its resource group analysis with its Superset tool, its database account svc_superset and a network policy for its pod; a change version adds the six cells. Each is approved by a qa person who did not make it and applied with apply.sh; then the first install. A builder builds and publishes, a viewer only views, and qa is refused. The exercise proves the decisions "Superset stage C" (7 November 2026, N1 to N11) and "Superset stage B" (D4, D6 to D8; see the decision record), and takes over from E24.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (OS account svieira), naming admin with --by; admin (admin), who drafts the change version in the Access Policy; a qa account, who approves both versions: planned as sergio_qa (decision N6), but sergio_qa held engineer from decision 17 of the previous install, so on 8 November 2026 the owner chose svieira (qa, a person other than admin's), named below; eng (engineer, a builder); a qp account as the viewer (on the previous install sergio_qp; on the current one make it with E1). On this install they are test accounts of one human: the attestation and the two-person rule are met by accounts, not by two people (decision N6a). Give each its own private browser window.

Before you start.

  • Commit A of stage C (the wiring) is deployed: ./deploy-infra.sh, ./apps/iam/deploy.sh, ./deploy-apps.sh --all (Superset skipped), and ./health-check.sh shows Superset roles SKIP and no failure; tests/iam-hosts.sh's superset client line passes.
  • IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is true (otherwise the install in step 8 is skipped).
  • ./apps/iam/apply.sh --status: no open version, the last apply finished, no policy break-glass; no account decision waits for qa; ./health-check.sh -c shows no failure (the apply's baseline refuses any).
  • The approver (svieira) is enabled, holds qa and has its own person_id, and no enabled account of its person holds a builder or viewer role (the apply refuses an approver whose person would gain from the version).
  • The qp account was created by the owner, approved by admin and confirmed by svieira in the User Manager.
  • Commit B, the policy, is on its branch, and the throwaway database run tests/iam-db-fixture.sh run with it passed.
  • A backup: ./apps/backup/backups.sh now, then verify. A skeleton version is never reverted.

The wiring first (commit A). Host operator, with no onboarding or run active: ./deploy-infra.sh, ./apps/iam/deploy.sh, ./deploy-apps.sh --all, ./health-check.sh, tests/iam-hosts.sh, then ./medcea.sh → Applications and → Policy. You should see: superset.<domain> among the certificate's names and SUPERSET_CLIENT_SECRET filled in config.env (not printed); iam-api restarting; [superset] skipped: Superset is not in the applied access policy, or no role is given a setting; Superset roles SKIP "no Superset deployment in medcea (./apps/superset/deploy.sh installs it once the applied access policy gives a role a Superset setting)"; the superset client lines of tests/iam-hosts.sh passing; the medcea.sh entries Install Superset, Re-render Superset's gate, Uninstall Superset, Superset stage C: after the skeleton version and Superset stage C: install Superset. Record the result in "Last done" before step 1.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by admin --reason "Superset stage C: host SUPERSET_DOMAIN, group analysis (tool superset), svc_superset (D7)" --from-git <commit B> --check-only, then the same without --check-only, answering y.
  2. svieira: Access Policy → Approval, open the skeleton version, read the header and the diff, tick "I did not run apply.sh --propose-skeleton for this version.", write a note, Approve.
  3. Host operator, back to back: git checkout <commit B>, ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by admin --check-only, then ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by admin, answering y.
  4. Host operator: ./medcea.sh → Policy → Superset stage C: after the skeleton version.
  5. admin: Access Policy → Changes → New draft from defaults, reason "Superset stage C: builders and viewers (D8, N1)"; look at Matrix and the diff; Submit. Then Who can…: group analysis, level U.
  6. svieira: Approval, open the change version, write a note, Approve.
  7. Host operator: ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by admin --check-only, then without --check-only, answering y.
  8. Host operator: ./medcea.sh → Policy → Superset stage C: install Superset.
  9. eng: portal → MedCEA Dashboard → Superset. In SQL Lab, on the MedCEA connection, run SELECT count(*) FROM medcea.measurement, then SELECT * FROM medcea.recipe_run LIMIT 1. Make a chart on a dataset of the MedCEA connection, put it on a new dashboard and publish the dashboard.
  10. The qp account: portal → MedCEA Dashboard → Superset; open the dashboard eng published.
  11. svieira: portal → MedCEA Dashboard → Superset.
  12. eng: Superset's Logout; then open the portal and the AI Workbench in the same window.
  13. eng: sign in to Superset again, leave it untouched for more than 5 minutes, then click anything.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: the chain verifies; --by admin resolved, holding a maker role; the skeleton widens only the platform's own reach (no person role gains anything); the checker is clean; then "version N (skeleton) submitted …", exit 0.
  • Step 2: the header (skeleton, --by admin, the commit, based on the applied version); no box saying the version widens a role you hold (the page shows one only when it does); "No role gains or loses anything." and "No cell changes."; the diff lists no waivers either, only system changes (Superset's host and client, svc_superset's read grants on master data and measurements and its row rule on measurement, the network policy's two sources) and the skeleton sections that change. Approve is enabled only once the page has checked the diff it shows, the box is ticked and a note written.
  • Step 3: the dry run passes the gate (an approved skeleton version from a commit HEAD contains) and the approval check; the summary shows the route table and grants changed, a network policy iam-superset, Superset's host with nobody admitted and no role's reach changed; nine checks as the baseline; after y the rollout prints SUPERSET_DOMAIN (superset): not deployed (./apps/superset/deploy.sh installs it), exit 0.
  • Step 4: the database deploy gives svc_superset its password and Secret db-svc-superset; the iam deploy restarts iam-api; the health check's Access policy version warns only that git differs from the applied matrix (the cells are in git already).
  • Step 5: the draft shows exactly six new cells (the three builders R, C, U; the three viewers R) and a clean checker; the diff has no system or skeleton part; Who can… names the three builders.
  • Step 6: no "This version widens a role you hold." box; the diff shows the six cells and one "Gains:" card for each builder and viewer role.
  • Step 7: the approver check passes (no account of svieira's person holds a role this version widens); the summary shows the route table, the host list and the grants targets changed (only role_widening's body: no privilege moves, so grants-json stays unchanged), Superset's host admitting nobody before and the six roles after, the new Superset tool target, the six roles' new reach, and the notice that access-api answers 503 for about a minute to account decisions that change into or out of bio_scientist, control_scientist, engineer, production_manager, qc or qp (make no such change in that minute); the rollout prints not deployed for Superset again; the git warning of step 4 is gone.
  • Step 8: the deploy logs the compiled sign-in roles (six), fills the wheel cache, creates database superset, runs the init Job and ends "Superset deployed: https://superset.<domain>"; the health check has 56 checks with Superset roles OK ("maps … from the access policy …; connection svc_superset"); the host check passes Superset's lines; the network test shows superset:8088 unreachable from a probe pod and Superset reachable through its address; the sign-in test (14 hosts with the Access Policy's, 168 sign-ins) lets the six roles in and refuses admin, qa, auditor, operator, maintenance and an account without a role with "No access to Superset"; verify lists db/superset.dump.
  • Step 9: Superset opens without a second sign-in page; SQL Lab is in the menu; the count runs; the query on recipe_run is refused by the database ("permission denied"); the chart and dashboard save and publish.
  • Step 10: the published dashboard opens; there is no SQL Lab, and + Chart is offered: viewers may make charts and dashboards of their own on the datasets they can read (decision of 7 November 2026). Note whether that held.
  • Step 11: a page "No access to Superset" naming the roles that may open it; no Superset user is created for svieira.
  • Step 12: Keycloak's "Do you want to log out?" page, then the portal and the AI Workbench both ask for a sign-in.
  • Step 13: the click goes through the platform sign-in without a password prompt and back into Superset.

The policy history holds, for the skeleton version, submitted (with the commit, the claimed --by person and the OS account), approved (the note begins with the attestation), the apply events and applied; for the change version the draft and save events, submitted, approved and applied (Access Policy → History, which also verifies the chain; ./apps/iam/apply.sh --audit N re-checks an applied version). The apply logs are logs/apply-policy-<time>.log, the Superset deploy's logs/app-superset-deploy-<time>.log. Keycloak records each sign-in (login events of realm medcea); Superset keeps its own log of sign-ins and actions in its database, which the nightly backup copies. The SQL Lab queries are not in the platform's record. Write the version numbers, the history event numbers and the health result under Last done, and add the evidence to the decision record row "Superset stage C".

Refusals worth trying.

  • Step 2 as admin: the Access Policy shows admin no Approval tab; only qa approves.
  • Step 6 as eng: the Access Policy's sign-in refuses an engineer ("No access to Access Policy").
  • Step 5 before step 4 has finished: the Access Policy still ships the previous skeleton, which has no group analysis, so the draft from defaults shows no Superset cells; and at step 6 Approve stays disabled with "The Policy service runs another skeleton than this host accepted: the host operator runs ./apps/iam/deploy.sh." Withdraw it, run step 4, draft again.
  • Step 2 with the box not ticked: Approve stays disabled; sent anyway, refused: "Tick the statement that you did not run apply.sh --propose-skeleton for this version."
  • Step 9: an UPDATE in SQL Lab is refused (the connection allows no data changes, and svc_superset may only read).
  • Step 10: opening https://superset.<domain>/sqllab/ directly as the viewer does not open SQL Lab.
  • Opening Superset as auditor: "No access to Superset", as for qa (decision D8).

Afterwards. Delete the chart and dashboard from step 9 if they were only for the exercise. Keep the qp account for later runs, or deactivate it in the User Manager. The versions stay applied: to take Superset away again, roll back to the skeleton version (./apps/iam/apply.sh --rollback-to N --by admin --reason "…", confirmed by qa), which stops Superset and keeps its data. Then run E20's Superset part.

E28 A fresh install comes up with Superset

Goal. See that a new install, made by one ./install.sh on a new config.env, puts every database client on its own database role, applies version 1 of the access policy and installs Superset with it, asking for sudo only where the infrastructure stage already does; and that an install whose config.env is older keeps its value of IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES and says what is still to do. The exercise proves the decision "Superset installed by default" (8 November 2026, see the decision record).

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the OS account that installs); the engineer account made at setup (ENGINEER_USER, a Superset builder) and the qa account made at setup (QA_USER, refused by Superset), each in its own private browser window.

Before you start.

  • A host with no MedCEA on it, or one you may wipe: ./install.sh --uninstall-all removes the platform and all its data (type uninstall to confirm). It also deletes logs/ and credentials-*.txt, so copy them off first if the old install's evidence is wanted. It keeps BACKUP_DIR, edge/provisioned/ and state/ (the policy files moved to state/retired-<time>-uninstall/). Take a backup just before (./apps/backup/backups.sh now, then verify): it holds the platform's, Keycloak's and Superset's databases and the workbench homes', Node-RED's and Grafana's volumes, and ./apps/backup/backups.sh restore-help gives the steps back. After the reinstall the new install's nightly run deletes folders older than BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS (except the newest complete one): restore within that time, or copy the folder off the host first.
  • At its last two questions: "Delete the platform CA (.ca/)? …" — answer no to keep it, so the new install reuses it ("Reusing existing CA (clients already trusting it keep working).") and browsers need nothing new; "Delete config.env (all settings and passwords)?" — answer yes, so the install makes a new one.
  • A clean checkout of the release you install (git status shows nothing): the iam deploy applies version 1 from the committed factory policy, and apply.sh refuses "apps/iam has uncommitted changes: version 1 is the committed factory policy; commit or stash them first".
  • At hand for the setup questions: a real ADMIN_EMAIL (of the domains, the setup refuses only special-use ones such as .local or .test, so a domain someone else owns passes, and mail for the admin would go there); the Docker Hub username and access token (checked live); the qa and engineer usernames (at least 3 characters: the setup accepts 2, but Keycloak refused such an account in E28, see Last done) and e-mails; Tailscale up, if the name <project> is to be the domain again.
  • The host reaches the internet, and its pods reach pypi.org: the first Superset install downloads three packages from PyPI (a firewall that lets the image registries through but blocks PyPI stops it there).
  • No other deploy runs; you are at a terminal (the install asks questions and for sudo).

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./install.sh. Answer the setup questions.
  2. Host operator, when it ends: grep '^IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=' config.env, ./apps/iam/apply.sh --status and ./health-check.sh.
  3. The engineer account: portal → MedCEA Dashboard → Superset.
  4. The qa account: portal → MedCEA Dashboard → Superset; then the Access Policy (https://policy.<domain>) → Confirm, version 1.
  5. Host operator: ./install.sh again, unchanged.

What you should see.

  • Step 1, the infrastructure stage: after the setup questions, the MedCEA logo, then "AppArmor rules for the cluster's containers..." and "Installing <project>-containerd-apparmor (MicroK8s's container profile + the stacked-peer rules; Ubuntu kernels from 7.0.0-41)..." (the uninstall removed these rules), with a sudo prompt that says why ("[sudo] password for <you> (AppArmor rules for the cluster's containers):"; it does not show while sudo still remembers your password from the uninstall in the same terminal, and the setup asks earlier if it must install a missing package or start Tailscale), then "AppArmor rules for containers in place (…)". The bootstrap installs MicroK8s with plain sudo. After it, "Superset's wheel cache folder..." and "Creating /var/lib/<project>/superset-wheels (mode 700, owner <you>)...", then "Superset wheel cache: …". The registry check ("[sudo] password for <you> (MicroK8s registry credentials):") and the wheel step ("[sudo] password for <you> (to create … for Superset's wheels):") have prompts of their own, but sudo is normally still unlocked from the bootstrap, so they seldom show. The applications stage asks for no sudo for Superset; the iam deploy applies version 1 and deploys iam-api and the Access Policy; Superset logs "Sign-in roles (compiled): …" (six roles), then "downloading into the wheel cache (PyPI, hash-checked): …" and "wheel cache complete (…)", and ends "Superset deployed: https://superset.<domain>". Then the line "IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is true: the infrastructure runs once more, so Grafana and pgAdmin move onto their own database roles (svc_grafana, rr_admin_login) now that the database lets them log in." and the stage "Infrastructure again (Grafana and pgAdmin onto their database roles)". The health check runs (64 checks); then "MedCEA is installed. Start at the service portal: …", "4 IAM switch(es) still false. To turn on the rest in order: ./medcea.sh → IAM switches → "Bring IAM to full enforcement".", "TRUST THE PLATFORM CERTIFICATE (once per device)" and the credentials box last. No "Still to do: Superset was skipped" line.
  • Step 2: IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES="true"; apply.sh --status says "state: version-1" and "applied: version 1 (bootstrap), claimed by person …, waiting for qa to confirm it (Policy UI → Confirm); last apply event bootstrap_applied …"; Database clients OK (every client on its own role) and Superset roles OK. These warn on every fresh install: the checks for the four switches still off (token checks, database roles, enforcement, personal MQTT credentials); Access policy version ("version 1 (bootstrap) is not confirmed by qa yet (the Policy UI)"; it stays after this exercise, because step 4's confirmation is refused until IAM_POSTGREST_JWT and IAM_DB_ROLES are true: qa confirms version 1 after Bring IAM to full enforcement); History chain anchor ("no anchor: the newest complete backup … predates this database …" while BACKUP_DIR holds the old install's backups, "no complete backup … yet" when it is empty) until the first nightly backup, or ./apps/backup/backups.sh now. In the first minutes Account drift may warn "drift not computed yet (the access pod started recently; …)". Backups judges the newest backup in BACKUP_DIR, the old install's, by its age.
  • Step 3: Superset opens after the platform sign-in, with SQL Lab in its menu.
  • Step 4: "No access to Superset". In the Access Policy, Confirm is enabled once the statement that you did not run apply.sh is ticked and a note is written; confirming then answers "Confirming is not possible on this platform yet (IAM_POSTGREST_JWT and IAM_DB_ROLES must be true). Ask the administrator." (by design until those two switches are on).
  • Step 5: every stage passes again, the infrastructure twice ("AppArmor rules for containers already in place (…)"); the wheel cache step creates nothing ("Superset's wheel cache folder..." and "Superset wheel cache: …" only).

The logs: logs/deploy-infra-<time>.log (twice: the second infrastructure run writes into its own), logs/deploy-apps-<time>.log (the iam deploy's bootstrap and the Superset deploy) and logs/health-check-<time>.log. The policy history holds bootstrap_applied for version 1 (Access Policy → History, or ./apps/iam/apply.sh --status). Superset's own database superset holds the engineer's Superset user from step 3; Keycloak records both sign-ins. Write the date, the commit (or release tag), the health result and each sudo prompt you were shown, with the reason it gave, under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • With an older config.env that has IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES="false", ./install.sh runs the infrastructure only once, Superset is skipped ("skipped: Superset needs IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=true (its data connection is svc_superset)"), and the install ends with "Still to do: Superset was skipped, it needs IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=true." naming the medcea.sh entry. A config.env with no line for the switch at all (from before Phase 2.5) is given IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES="false" by the setup, which says so: "Note: config.env had no IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES line; it is set to false, as this install has run (a new config.env has true)."
  • SUPERSET_WHEEL_DIR set to a folder inside the volumes' directory (/var/snap/microk8s/common/default-storage/…): ./deploy-infra.sh stops at the wheel cache step ("is inside the volumes' directory …: choose another folder (config.env)."), before Helm or Keycloak change.
  • sudo ./deploy-infra.sh: the step creates nothing ("Running as root: Superset's wheel cache is not created here (the init containers run as its owner, never root)."); the Superset deploy, run as the deploying account, creates it.
  • pgAdmin, signed in as the administrator, on the fresh install: an UPDATE or a CREATE TABLE is refused ("permission denied"): pgAdmin holds rr_admin's grants only. Fixes go through psql in the PostgreSQL pod.
  • If the iam deploy could not apply version 1 (its bootstrap waits, and the iam deploy warns why), Superset is skipped with "skipped: no version of the access policy is applied yet (state empty), and Superset deploys only from an applied one: run ./apps/superset/deploy.sh once ./apps/iam/deploy.sh has applied version 1 (./apps/iam/apply.sh --status)", and the install ends with the matching "Still to do" line.

Afterwards. Keep the install, or remove it again with ./install.sh --uninstall-all, which also removes Superset's wheel cache (and /var/lib/<project> when that is left empty), asking for sudo when it must. To go on with the access controls, run ./medcea.sh → IAM switches → Bring IAM to full enforcement; it skips IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES, which is already true.

E29 A newer kernel with the AppArmor rules

Goal. See that ./deploy-infra.sh installs the AppArmor rules for the cluster's containers, that they come back after MicroK8s rewrites its profile, and that with them the platform runs on an Ubuntu kernel from 7.0.0-41, which without them stops PostgreSQL, nginx and Mosquitto. The exercise proves the decision "AppArmor rules for containers on newer Ubuntu kernels" (8 November 2026, see the decision record) and is what lets the host leave kernel 7.0.0-38.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the OS account that deploys, with sudo). No platform account.

Before you start.

  • The host runs on the kernel it is held on (7.0.0-38), and ./health-check.sh passes; a nightly backup from today (./apps/backup/backups.sh list), or take one with ./apps/backup/backups.sh now.
  • No onboarding run, no recipe run and no other deploy is active; nobody is using the platform (step 3 restarts containerd, step 5 reboots the host).
  • The newer kernel is installed (ls /boot/vmlinuz-*). You are at the host's console or have a way back if it does not boot (a reboot can be undone only from the GRUB menu).

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./deploy-infra.sh.
  2. Host operator: ./health-check.sh; systemctl status <project>-containerd-apparmor.path; grep -A5 'medcea: stacked-peer' /etc/apparmor.d/cri-containerd.apparmor.d.
  3. Host operator: sudo systemctl restart snap.microk8s.daemon-containerd, wait a minute, then journalctl -u <project>-containerd-apparmor.service -b --no-pager | tail and step 2's grep again.
  4. Host operator: ./deploy-infra.sh once more.
  5. Host operator: reboot and choose the newer kernel in the GRUB menu (Advanced options), without changing the default.
  6. Host operator, about ten minutes after the boot (pgAdmin's start takes that long): uname -r; cat /proc/$(pgrep -f 'postgres: checkpointer')/attr/apparmor/current; journalctl -k -b | grep 'DENIED.*operation="signal"' | grep -v check-status | wc -l; ./health-check.sh.
  7. Host operator, only if step 6 is as below: make the newer kernel the default (GRUB_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub, sudo update-grub) and sudo apt-mark unhold the older kernel's packages.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: "AppArmor rules for the cluster's containers..." with one sudo prompt ("[sudo] password for <you> (AppArmor rules for the cluster's containers):"), then "AppArmor rules for containers in place (<project>-containerd-apparmor)."; nothing restarts.
  • Step 2: Container AppArmor OK, naming the kernel, restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1, "no signal denials since" and "host profile(s) off: mosquitto"; the path unit active; the four rules after the marker line.
  • Step 3: the unit ran again ("wrote /etc/apparmor.d/cri-containerd.apparmor.d (MicroK8s's profile + the stacked-peer rules)", "loaded cri-containerd.apparmor.d with the stacked-peer rules"), and the rules are in the file again although MicroK8s copied its own over it.
  • Step 4: "AppArmor rules for containers already in place", no sudo prompt for this step.
  • Step 6: the newer kernel; the checkpointer labelled cri-containerd.apparmor.d//&unconfined (enforce) (the stacked label, which the rules now cover); 0 refused signals besides check-status lines from before the rules loaded; every health check OK, Container AppArmor first.

The logs: logs/deploy-infra-<time>.log (steps 1 and 4), logs/health-check-<time>.log (steps 2 and 6); the unit's own runs in the journal (journalctl -u <project>-containerd-apparmor.service), the kernel's refusals in journalctl -k. Nothing is recorded in the platform database. Write the date, the commit, both kernel versions, the refusal count of step 6 and the health result under Last done, and the result in the decision record's row.

Refusals worth trying.

  • With the unit stopped and disabled (sudo systemctl disable --now <project>-containerd-apparmor.path), step 3 leaves MicroK8s's profile without the rules, and ./health-check.sh fails Container AppArmor ("… lacks the rules"; or "is not installed" when both units are disabled). On the newer kernel PostgreSQL's pod is then refused its signals within minutes; ./deploy-infra.sh puts everything back.
  • Installing Mosquitto on the host (/usr/sbin/mosquitto) keeps Ubuntu's host profile on: the unit warns "… is installed on this host, so profile mosquitto stays on", and on the newer kernel the health check names the container it attaches to.

Afterwards. If step 6 is not as above, reboot into the older kernel (the default has not changed) and keep the hold. The rules go only with MicroK8s: ./install.sh --uninstall-all removes the units and turns the host profile back on.

Last done. 9 November 2026, all seven steps; steps 1 to 4 on kernel 7.0.0-38, working tree on a1802d6 (not yet committed): steps 1 to 4 passed. Step 1: ./deploy-infra.sh (logs/deploy-infra-20261109-102010.log) installed medcea-containerd-apparmor ("AppArmor rules for containers in place"). Step 2: the path unit active, the last run success, the marker and the four rules in the profile; ./health-check.sh all 57 checks OK. Step 3: after sudo systemctl restart snap.microk8s.daemon-containerd (10:59:22) the unit ran within 4 seconds ("wrote …", "loaded cri-containerd.apparmor.d with the stacked-peer rules") and the rules were back in the file; the journal also shows a run at 10:47:55, the same repair after a containerd start nobody asked for. Step 4: ./deploy-infra.sh said "already in place" with no sudo prompt (logs/deploy-infra-20261109-111011.log); logs/health-check-20261109-111344.log: all 57 checks OK. Two installer faults were found and fixed on the way: the host package check stopped the first attempt (a test with || in infra/lib-prereqs.sh, "ERROR: is still missing"; it now also writes logs/prereqs-<time>.log), and the first step-4 run stopped at the portal (logs/deploy-infra-20261109-110119.log: Superset's card and section 9 both restarted the portal within one second, which kubectl refuses). Step 5: rebooted into 7.0.0-43-generic from the GRUB menu (booted 11:36:51). The host now boots 7.0.0-43 by default.

E30 medcea.sh: dialog boxes

Goal. See that ./medcea.sh at a terminal shows its menus and questions as dialog boxes headed by the status header (and the MedCEA logo on a large terminal), that the header matches the host, that a command still runs on the plain terminal and is then summed up in a box with its result, its log and the end of its output, that --plain brings back the numbered questions, and that the old name ./guide.sh only forwards. The exercise proves the decision "Dialog boxes for ./guide.sh, the name ./medcea.sh, the end-of-command box and the MedCEA logo" (9 November 2026, see the decision record); how the boxes work is in Dialog boxes and the status header.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the OS account that deploys), at a terminal on the host (local or over SSH). No platform account.

Before you start.

  • whiptail and script are installed (command -v whiptail script; Ubuntu ships both) and the terminal is at least 100 columns by 40 lines (make the window large; step 1 needs it for the logo).
  • No deploy is running; you know the last health check's result (ls -t logs/health-check-*.log | head -1) and git log -1 --oneline.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./medcea.sh --dry-run. Read the logo and the status header on the first menu.
  2. Move with the arrow keys to Health and tests and press Enter; in that menu choose Route table vs code (offline).
  3. Read the confirmation box and choose Yes; then OK on the next box.
  4. Back in the area menu press Esc; on the first menu choose Infrastructure → Publish the manual to the portal and press Enter on the confirmation without moving.
  5. Choose Back to the menu, then Back, then Quit.
  6. Make the window small (24 lines) and run ./medcea.sh --dry-run again; Quit. Make it large again.
  7. Host operator: ./medcea.sh (not a dry run); Health and tests → Route table vs code (offline) → Yes. When it has finished, read the box that follows, press Tab and scroll its text with the arrow keys, then choose Menu, then Esc and Quit.
  8. Host operator: ./medcea.sh --plain --dry-run, type q; then echo q | ./medcea.sh --dry-run.
  9. Host operator: ./guide.sh --help | head -3.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: a dark box titled "What do you want to do?", the line "MedCEA | <host> | <kernel> | <commit>" above it; at the top of its text the MedCEA logo (the herb, the MedCEA lettering with "Controlled Environment Agriculture for Medicinal Plants and Fungi", the mushroom), then the header: Host and Kernel as uname -n and uname -r say; Git with your branch and git log -1's commit (and dirty when git status lists anything); Health with the newest log's summary line and its age; Policy with the applied version as version=N kind=K; Lock: free; DRY RUN: nothing is run and config.env is not changed. The entries have the numbers of the numbered mode, as "label — purpose"; the buttons are Select and Quit.
  • Step 2: the area's box has a Back button and no logo.
  • Step 3: the box "Run this read-only command?" holds the plan (python3 tests/iam-routes-diff.py, Kind read-only, Deploy lock no) with Yes selected; then a box "Dry run" with "[dry run] not executed: python3 tests/iam-routes-diff.py".
  • Step 4: Esc returns to the first menu (with the logo again). The box "This changes the platform" has No selected, so Enter answers no: the next box says "Cancelled; nothing was run." with the buttons Back to the menu and Quit.
  • Step 5: medcea.sh ends with "Bye." on the terminal.
  • Step 6: the first menu has the header but no logo (no room).
  • Step 7: no Dry run line in the header; after Yes the screen clears, shows $ python3 tests/iam-routes-diff.py, the script's own output and "Finished: exit code 0."; then a box titled Finished: exit code 0 with the line $ python3 tests/iam-routes-diff.py → Finished: exit code 0, "The last lines of its output:" and the script's last lines without colour codes (no Log: line: this script writes no log), and the buttons Menu and Quit; Menu brings back the area's box.
  • Step 8: the numbered menu ("1) Install and uninstall" …, "b) back q) quit", "Choice:") both times, and "Bye."; at a terminal the numbered mode first prints the coloured logo once (the piped one in the second command prints none).
  • Step 9: "guide.sh is now ./medcea.sh (this name will be removed in a later release)", then medcea.sh's own help ("medcea.sh — the MedCEA menus …", "./medcea.sh [--dry-run] [--help]").

Nothing is recorded in the platform: the boxes, the logo and the status header only read files on the host. The commands medcea.sh runs log as before (here none: tests/iam-routes-diff.py writes no log), and the status header reads logs/health-check-*.log and state/policy-applied.yaml without changing them. The copy of the command's output that the end box is built from lives only while the box is built (a mode-600 file in medcea.sh's own temporary folder, deleted at once); nothing of it is kept. Write the date, the commit and what the header and the end box showed under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • In a dry run, Operators and units → Assign units to an operator, then OK on the empty username box: the box comes back with "'': letters, digits and . _ @ + -, starting with a letter or digit" above the question, because a required answer cannot be skipped. Now press Esc: the area menu comes back saying "Cancelled; nothing was run." and no plan was shown.
  • Applications → Uninstall components, in a dry run, and Esc at "Names or numbers … (Enter = all)": "Cancelled; nothing was run.", never a plan to remove every component (only Enter on OK means all).
  • Install and uninstall → Uninstall the infrastructure, in a dry run: a box titled DESTRUCTIVE; typing y cancels ("Cancelled; nothing was run."), only yes reaches the dry-run line.
  • Start ./apps/backup/backups.sh now (it takes the deploy lock) in a second terminal and, while it runs, open any menu in medcea.sh: the header says held by <command> (pid N). The next menu after it has finished says free.
  • Not a dry run: Health and tests → Route table vs code (offline) → Yes, and press Ctrl+C while it runs (it is quick: try a longer read-only command such as Health check if you miss it): only the command stops, and the box says Failed: exit code 130; medcea.sh goes on (Menu).
  • ./guide.sh --bogus: the note, then "[medcea.sh] unknown argument '--bogus' (./medcea.sh --help)", exit code 2 (echo $?): the old name only forwards, options and exit code included.
  • MEDCEA_TUI_FORCE=1 ./medcea.sh: refused with "MEDCEA_TUI_FORCE needs MEDCEA_TUI_TTY=<file>" (a test hook, exit 2).

Afterwards. Nothing to undo. To keep the numbered questions, run ./medcea.sh --plain or set MEDCEA_PLAIN=1 in your shell. Replace ./guide.sh in your own notes and scripts by ./medcea.sh.

Fixed in 9813ea2, which strips them in C.UTF-8 whatever the terminal's locale. E31 Read the Phase 5 health checks

Goal. See that ./health-check.sh now runs 61 checks (64 since the second round of the same day, E32), read the four new ones (Policy loaded by services, Realm signing keys, Keycloak client scopes, Application network policies) and the changed ones, and see two of them react to a change. The exercise proves the decision "Health checks of Phase 5: proving the applied policy is the one in force" (9 November 2026, see the decision record); what each check means is in The health check.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the OS account that deploys, in the microk8s group), at a terminal in the repository. No platform account: the checks read the cluster and the databases, never through a sign-in.

Before you start.

  • The checkout holds the Phase 5 checks (grep -cE '\| *(iamloaded|jwks|kcscopes|iamnetpol) *\|' health-checks.conf says 4), and the last ./deploy-infra.sh ran with the config.env you have now.
  • No deploy is running; every IAM switch is true (otherwise the switch checks WARN, as they should). Note git log -1 --oneline.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./health-check.sh. Read the summary line, then the lines Policy loaded by services, Realm signing keys, Keycloak client scopes and Application network policies.
  2. Host operator: ./health-check.sh -v, and read the detail of those four and of Database grants, PostgREST tokens, Service enforcement and Access policy history.
  3. Host operator: add an empty line at the end of one file in apps/node-red/flows/ (do not commit it), run ./health-check.sh and read Node-RED flows vs git; then git checkout -- apps/node-red/flows and run it once more.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: "All 61 checks passed." (64 since the second round, E32; or a count of OK, warnings and failures out of that many checks). The four new lines OK.
  • Step 2: Policy loaded by services: "N pods in M services load routes <12 hex digits> (applied_version <the applied version>, information only)", followed by "; K not deployed (…)" for a service not installed; the digest is the one kubectl -n <namespace> get cm medcea-iam-lib -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.medcea/routes-digest}' prints. Realm signing keys: "N signing key(s) (<key id>) equal the realm's; jwks-sig.json = jwks.json's signing keys" (key ids only, never a key). Keycloak client scopes: "15 clients: groups and medcea-identity default on each (10 of them reach a platform API)". Application network policies: "N NetworkPolicies of the application pods, the compiled set". Database grants names "IAM_DB_ROLES=true: every grantee, RLS, triggers and classification". PostgREST tokens ends "(realm key ids: jwks)". Service enforcement ends "switches match config.env". Access policy history OK with no note on verify_chain().
  • Step 3: Node-RED flows vs git WARN, ending "1 flow file(s) not committed to git: <file> (W1 covers committed flows: commit them)"; after the checkout OK again.

The log logs/health-check-<time>.log of each run. Nothing is written anywhere else: the checks take no deploy lock, read Keycloak's database and the platform database in read-only transactions (so no sign-in or admin event in Keycloak), read each pod with one kubectl exec that prints only a digest and a version, and print no secret. Write the date, the commit, the summary line of step 1 and any WARN or FAIL under Last done, and the result in the decision record's row.

Refusals worth trying.

  • Only while nobody uses the platform: microk8s kubectl -n <namespace> delete netpol iam-monitor, then ./health-check.sh: Application network policies FAIL, "IAM_NETPOL=true, missing: iam-monitor: those pods admit any caller in the cluster (./deploy-infra.sh)", and the run exits 1. ./deploy-infra.sh --policy-only puts it back (it prints "[policy-only] netpol: re-rendered"), and the check is OK again.
  • Right after a deploy that changes the route table (an apply.sh of a version with new routes), Policy loaded by services may WARN "… since N s (the kubelet syncs within 120 s)" for up to two minutes; a pod still behind after that is a FAIL naming its deploy script. Do not cause this on purpose; note it if you see it.

Afterwards. Nothing to undo once git status -- apps/node-red/flows lists nothing and every check is OK. A WARN or FAIL you did not cause goes to the person who runs the platform with the line's text: each one names the command that fixes it.

Step 2 (-v, after the manual was republished): Policy loaded by services “6 pods in 6 services load routes a22cd58f318d (applied_version 16, information only)”; Realm signing keys “1 signing key(s) (RI_fOOPx1T1J) equal the realm’s; jwks-sig.json = jwks.json’s signing keys”; Keycloak client scopes “15 clients: groups and medcea-identity default on each (10 of them reach a platform API)”; Application network policies “9 NetworkPolicies of the application pods, the compiled set”; Database grants named the IAM_DB_ROLES=true set, PostgREST tokens ended “(realm key ids: jwks)”, Service enforcement “switches match config.env”; all 61 OK (logs/health-check-20261109-225003.log). Step 3: Node-RED flows vs git WARN “1 flow file(s) not committed to git: message-processing.json (W1 covers committed flows: commit them)”, “60 OK, 1 warning(s), 0 failures — 61 checks” (…-225341.log); after git checkout all 61 OK again (…-225600.log). The network-policy refusal was not tried.

E32 Read the second round of Phase 5 checks

Goal. Deploy the access-api that computes the account drift, see that ./health-check.sh now runs 64 checks, and read the three new ones: Account drift, History chain anchor and Database catalog. The exercise proves the decision "Health checks of Phase 5, round 2: account drift, chain anchor, catalog" (9 November 2026, see the decision record); what each check means is in The health check.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the OS account that deploys, in the microk8s group, and the account that ran ./apps/backup/deploy.sh, so it can read BACKUP_DIR), at a terminal in the repository. No platform account for the steps; a qa or admin person may open the User Manager's Decisions tab to compare its red banner with the counts.

Before you start.

  • The checkout holds the new checks (grep -cE '\| *(iamdrift|iamanchor|iamcatalog) *\|' health-checks.conf says 3). Note git log -1 --oneline.
  • At least one complete nightly backup made since IAM 4.5 exists: ./apps/backup/backups.sh list shows it (otherwise run ./apps/backup/backups.sh now first).
  • No deploy is running and nobody is in the middle of a decision in the User Manager: step 1 restarts its pod.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./deploy-infra.sh. Besides its usual work it records the platform admin (ADMIN_USER) as a seeded account (an account_seeded fact, as for the first qa person and the first engineer), so the drift report explains the admin role ./deploy-infra.sh gave it.
  2. Host operator: ./apps/access/deploy.sh. It takes the deploy lock and restarts the access pod with the drift report.
  3. Wait for the first computation: it runs as soon as the pod has started, so one minute after the deploy ends is enough (if Keycloak was not ready yet, it tries again 2 minutes later).
  4. Host operator: ./health-check.sh -v. Read the summary line, then the lines Account drift, History chain anchor and Database catalog.

What you should see.

  • Steps 1 and 2: both deploys end without an error; the first prints "account fact(s) recorded (account_seeded)" once for the admin; before step 2, Account drift WARNs "this access-api predates the drift report: ./apps/access/deploy.sh".
  • Step 4: "All 64 checks passed." or a count of OK, warnings and failures out of 64 checks.
  • Account drift OK: "N accounts: 0 unexplained roles, 0 failed compensations, 0 enabled while pending, 0 unrecorded; computed S s ago (every 600 s)". Counts only, never a name. On this install two other results are possible and are not faults of the check: FAIL "N platform role(s) no confirmed decision or signed-off review explains (User Manager → Decisions)" when the Decisions tab's red banner already lists unexplained roles (for example a role set in Keycloak's console; the role ./deploy-infra.sh gave an account it seeded is explained by its seed fact), and WARN "N enabled account(s) with no request, decision or status record and not seeded: review them (User Manager → Users)" for accounts such as the test accounts of the 1 November install. The banner names the same accounts. Write down the counts; explaining them (a decision, or for a role a signed-off access review) is a separate decision. A signed-off review does not clear an unrecorded account. If BACKUP_DIR still holds the newest backup of an earlier install, History chain anchor WARNs "no anchor: the newest complete backup … predates this database …" until the next nightly backup.
  • History chain anchor OK: "event N has the hash backup <folder> recorded (H h old), M event(s) since", where <folder> is the newest folder ./apps/backup/backups.sh list shows. Run as another OS account it WARNs "no anchor: cannot read … (BACKUP_DIR, mode 700): run this as the account that ran ./apps/backup/deploy.sh".
  • Database catalog OK: "every object owned by medcea_owner, N iam and all append-only triggers ENABLE ALWAYS, every medcea view security_invoker". This is its first run on a live database: a FAIL naming objects (for example an extension's functions in one of the four schemas) is a finding to report, not something to fix in the exercise.

The logs logs/app-access-deploy-<time>.log and logs/health-check-<time>.log. The checks write nothing: they take no deploy lock, read the database in read-only sessions, read BACKUP_DIR without sudo, and read the drift counts with one kubectl exec into the access pod that prints numbers only. access-api computes the drift in a read-only session and changes nothing in Keycloak. Write the date, the commit, the summary line and the three lines' texts under Last done, and the result in the decision record's row.

Refusals worth trying.

  • Harmless: ANCHOR_MAX_H=0 ./health-check.sh. History chain anchor WARNs "event N has the hash backup <folder> recorded, but the newest complete backup <folder> is H h old (over 0 h: ./apps/backup/backups.sh list)". The next run without the variable is OK again.
  • Only if an admin event in Keycloak is acceptable: create an account in Keycloak's console in the platform realm, enabled, with no role (it can open nothing: the portal refuses an account without a role), wait up to 10 minutes and run ./health-check.sh: Account drift WARNs one more unrecorded account. Disable the account in the console (accounts are disabled, never deleted); a disabled account is not counted, so after the next computation (up to 10 minutes) the count is back.
  • Do not disable a trigger, change an owner or edit a backup's MANIFEST to see a FAIL: tests/test_health_phase5b.py proves those texts offline, and tests/iam-db.sh proves the catalog statements on the throwaway test database.

Afterwards. Nothing to undo, but disabling the account you may have created in the second refusal. A FAIL or WARN you did not cause goes to the person who runs the platform with the line's text; for account drift, a qa person reviews the accounts in the User Manager.

E33 The Configuration UI shows what your role may do

Goal. See that each role is offered only the changes the database accepts from it, and that a panel the role may not read says so in plain words instead of failing. The exercise proves the decision "The Configuration UI follows the database's own answer" (12 November 2026, see the decision record); how the page decides is in What your role sees.

Accounts and roles. The three accounts of this install: admin (admin), eng (engineer) and qa_user (qa), one after the other in the same browser (sign out in between), or in three private windows. The host operator, at a terminal, for the record. No separation of duties is exercised: nothing is changed.

Before you start.

  • The Configuration UI deployed from this change (./apps/frontend/deploy.sh), with IAM_POSTGREST_JWT=true and IAM_DB_ROLES=true: while IAM_DB_ROLES is false everyone is shown the same buttons, and the exercise shows nothing.
  • At least one unit and one recipe exist (any status). Note git log -1 --oneline.

Steps.

  1. admin: open the Configuration UI and the Units tab. Look at the Production Units header and a unit's row, then scroll to Recipe ↔ Unit Permissions. Open a unit's Zones.
  2. admin: open the Locations, Devices, Control Models and Recipes tabs.
  3. eng: open the Units tab. Click Edit on a unit, then Cancel without saving. Scroll to Recipe ↔ Unit Permissions.
  4. eng: open the Recipes tab and a draft recipe's Edit, then ← Back; open Control Models.
  5. qa_user: open the Units tab and Recipe ↔ Unit Permissions, then the Recipes tab and a recipe's View, then the Approvals tab.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: no Edit on the unit rows, no + New Unit and no ↑ Import; ↓ Export and Zones stay. The Recipe ↔ Unit Permissions panel says "Your role does not read recipes or their unit permissions." (no longer "Load failed: permission denied for table control_algorithm"). The zones show without + Add Zone or Edit.
  • Step 2: no + New Location, Edit, + Add Record, ⚡ Onboard Device, + New Parameter Set or + New Recipe; ↓ Export offers only Download to Local Machine. Control Algorithms says "Your role does not read control algorithms." once the services enforce (IAM_ENFORCE=true; before, the list shows, without Save), Parameter Sets says your role does not read them, and the Recipes tab "Your role does not read recipes.", with no red message and without Show retired or ↓ Export All.
  • Step 3: Edit, + New Unit and ↑ Import are there and the unit form opens. The Recipe ↔ Unit grid is read-only: ticks and dashes, no circles to click, and the header says "Read-only for your role". Assignments are the production_manager's: an engineer holds no right to change them.
  • Step 4: Edit, ⎘ Copy, + Add Step and Retire… on a draft recipe; the algorithms' Save and + New Parameter Set on Control Models.
  • Step 5: the grid read-only, as for eng; every recipe opens with View, its form greyed and without Save, ⎘ Copy, Retire… or + Add Step, and an approved recipe's note reads only "Approved: this recipe is frozen." (no ⎘ Copy to point to); the Approvals tab with its queue.

Nothing is recorded in the platform's records: the page's questions change no row (they name a record that does not exist), so the row-change log, the approvals and the policy history are unchanged. PostgreSQL writes one line per question it refused to its server log, for example "ERROR: permission denied for table cea_unit" for admin when the page opens; the host operator may read them in the PostgreSQL pod's log (rdbms-postgresql-0). Write the date, the commit and what each account saw under Last done, and the result in the decision record's row.

Refusals worth trying.

  • None through the page: the buttons are gone. The database still refuses: as admin, in the browser's developer console on the Configuration UI, fetch('/api/cea_unit?unit_id=eq.-1', {method: 'PATCH', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Prefer': 'return=minimal'}, body: '{"unit_code": null}'}).then(async r => console.log(r.status, await r.text())) prints a refusal status (401: PostgREST counts the request as anonymous) and {"code": "42501", …, "message": "permission denied for table cea_unit"}. As eng the same request prints 204 with an empty body and changes nothing (no unit has the id -1).
  • As eng, change a step of an approved recipe from the developer console (PATCH /api/recipe_line?recipe_id=eq.<id>): the database refuses it with "draft_only: the recipe of this line is not a draft; a change starts a new draft"; on the page the same refusal reads "This recipe is no longer a draft (approved or retired meanwhile), so its steps cannot change. ⎘ Copy makes a new draft."

Afterwards. Nothing to undo: no step saves anything. Sign out of each account.

Adding an exercise

Every change a user would notice gets an exercise in this chapter, in the same piece of work as the change: a new screen, button, rule or refusal. Extend an exercise when the change belongs to it; add a new one (E9, E10 and so on) when it does not.

  1. Write it in the form of How every exercise is written, all nine parts. Take the screen, tab, button and field names and the refusal texts from the code, not from memory.
  2. Add its row to Exercises at a glance: exercise, roles, what it proves, last done ("Not yet").
  3. After the change is deployed, run the exercise on the platform.
  4. Write the date and the result under Last done and in the summary row, with the record numbers the screens showed (approval, decision, pending change). Never write a number you did not see.
  5. When the exercise is evidence that a control works, record it in the decision record as well, and list anything it found in known gaps.

Reference

Lookup tables for everyday use: the web addresses and who may open them, the roles each application admits, the access levels and resource groups of the access policy, the settings an administrator may change, the scripts on the platform host, the health checks, and the abbreviations used in this manual. The tables describe the platform as of IAM 2.6, deployed report-only on 31 October 2026, with the access policy at its default version.

Web addresses

Every web application has its own address, <name>.$DOMAIN, set by a *_DOMAIN setting in config.env. Every address except the access request form signs you in through Keycloak first. "Who can open it" is the list python3 apps/iam/compiler/cli.py hosts prints from the access policy. Where the gate is not compiled from the policy yet, the last column says what applies today.

The access policy also names an Access Policy host (POLICY_DOMAIN, for admin, qa, qp and auditor). Its address is POLICY_DOMAIN (policy.$DOMAIN); it is deployed by ./apps/iam/deploy.sh since IAM 4.3, and on a fresh install from 8 November 2026 on, since IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is then true. With IAM_GATES="false" the compiled hosts fall back to the pre-policy list operator, qa, auditor, admin. Sensor and control boards do not use a web address: they reach the MQTT broker over TLS on port 31884 of the platform host (the plain port 31883 is closed since 5 November 2026).

Roles and applications

The same data as the table above, one row per role: "yes" means the access policy admits the role to that application. For device onboarding, maintenance may only re-onboard into a slot that already exists. In Grafana, engineer is Editor and the other roles marked "yes" are Viewer. In the Monitor, the two scientist roles read telemetry but not runs. In Superset, "builder" means charts, dashboards and SQL Lab (Superset's Alpha), "viewer" dashboards and charts on the datasets it may read, without SQL Lab (Gamma). Roles qc and qp are defined for later use.

Opening an application is only the first gate. What you may do on the page is decided by your access levels on each resource group, checked by the service and by the database.

Access levels

Every cell of the access policy holds zero or more of these levels. A level that "includes" others gives them too.

LetterNameIncludesMeaning
NNoneNo access. The role does not see the resource at all. The default for every cell.
RReadSee the resource, change nothing.
XRead and exportRRead, and take a copy out of the platform through the Database Management export. Each export is recorded with who exported which objects and when.
CCreateRAdd new records; never change existing ones. Used for appending to regulated data and audit trails.
UUpdateC, RCreate and change records, within the group's constraint. On recipes and controllers only while the record is a draft. Removing a configuration record means setting it to "retired", never deleting it. Never given to a person on regulated or history data.
AApproveRApprove or release another person's work. The approver must be a different person from the author. In this version an approval is an attributable, time-stamped record, not a 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature.
OOperateRStart, stop or trigger a process (execute a run, stop it, trigger a schedule) without changing its definition.
KConfigureAdminister the tool without the content it holds. On accounts it means reading and changing account records, which are personal data. Held only by admin.
DDeleteRemove platform components and releases on the host. Never data. Held only by admin.

Resource groups

Each row of the access policy is a resource group: tables, service routes, web pages and MQTT topics that belong together. The class decides the rules that always apply to the group.

ClassLabelRule
regulatedRegulated dataRecords produced while making product. Created once, never changed or deleted by anyone; corrections are new records.
historyAudit historyAppend-only trails of who did what, including approval records and export logs. Written by the system only; readable by reviewers.
personalPersonal dataAccounts, names, e-mail addresses, unit assignments and access decisions. Administered by admin, confirmed by qa, readable by reviewers.
configConfigurationMaster data, recipes, controllers, schedules, settings, dashboards and tools. Changed under the group's approval rule.
Group keyLabelClass

user_managerUser Manager pageconfig

master_dataMaster data (locations, units, zones, components)config
devicesDevices and provisioningconfig
onboardingDevice onboarding (edge wizard)config
device_historyDevice placement historyhistory
recipesRecipes and recipe-to-unit assignmentconfig
controllersControllers and parameter setsconfig
controllers_statePersisted controller state (Q-tables)regulated
runsRecipe runs and cycle runsregulated
schedulesSchedulesconfig
scheduler_settingsScheduler settings (log retention)config
measurementsTelemetryregulated

mqtt_controlCommand and setpoint topicsregulated
